### Section 1 The chain is running now
**OBS** `hypridle` is live on this host (S205): the process probe prints pid 1667,
and the user journal holds two `Started hypridle.` lines dated 2026-10-23, the later
at 22:14:11 - a restart, not a first start.
**OBS** The declared chain is a screensaver at 150 seconds and a lock at 152
(S205), and both fire the desktop's own lock command.
### Section 2 Two probes disagree, and the disagreement is the finding
**OBS** `systemctl --user is-active hypridle` answers `inactive` (S205) while the

scope unit rather than as a `hypridle` service, so a reading taken from the unit
name is a probe artefact. The lane's own earlier note, `knowledge/idle-lock-plane.md`
(a dated 2026-10-14 point sample), recorded the daemon's absence; this round's
measurement does not contradict it - it shows the process running on 2026-10-24, and
the difference is a state that has moved, not a false record.
### Section 3 What this does not license
**UNK** No lock, screensaver or suspend transition was triggered or observed. The
chain is armed; whether it fires, and what the operator prefers, stay unknown.

### Section 1 The setup path asks nothing about the idle lock
**OBS** The desktop's post-login questionnaire is a one-shot script (S203): it runs a
fixed list of twelve first-run scripts when its mode file is present, and the list is
battery monitor, internal monitor, sudoers cleanup, firewall, DNS resolver, GNOME
theme, swayosd, primary paste, text scaling, elephant, welcome and wifi. None of the
twelve asks about the idle lock.
**OBS** And the operator never exercised the toggle afterwards (S204): the user
journal holds zero `omarchy-toggle` invocations.
### Section 2 What this closes and what it does not
**OBS** Two independent negatives agree. The setup path offers no idle-lock choice,
and the toggle was never run in any session the journal still keeps.
**UNK** Whether the operator would rather the idle lock were off. No source can
answer it; the answer is one sentence from the person who owns the machine.
### Section 3 The scope of this entry
The package's round-12 text framed the finding as "the desktop never offers the
choice". That framing is too broad and is corrected here: this entry is about the
**setup path** only. The running interface does offer the choice, and
`corpus/knowledge/idle-lock-offered-in-the-bar-r15.md` (adopted in the same round)
states that correction with its own evidence.

### Section 1 Two independent surfaces offer the choice
**OBS** The bar carries a dedicated module for it, and clicking that module runs the
toggle (S206): `custom/idle-indicator` opens at line 207 of the bar's configuration
and its `on-click` is `omarchy-toggle-idle` at line 208.
**OBS** The desktop's own menu lists the same toggle and dispatches it to the same
command (S208): `Idle Lock` appears among the menu's toggle options at line 207, and
the case arm `*Idle*) omarchy-toggle-idle ;;` is at line 212.
**INF** The operator is asked, in the interface they use every session, whether the
lock should be on. The premise that the desktop never offers the choice was drawn
from the setup path alone; it is corrected here.
### Section 2 The desktop names the two states itself
**OBS** The indicator does more than toggle (S207): it asks whether `hypridle` is
running, renders nothing when it is, and renders an icon whose tooltip reads
`Idle lock disabled` when it is not.
**OBS** And the offer is not new (S209): four dated copies of the bar's configuration
each carry the `omarchy-toggle-idle` handler, the oldest dated 2026-10-03 on this
host.
### Section 3 Why the choice leaves no trace
**OBS** The desktop keeps the state of its configuration toggles in one directory,
and it holds entries for other toggles - but not for the idle lock (S210): the
directory holds 2 files and 0 of them name the idle lock.
**INF** So the absence of an entry is not evidence that the operator never
considered the choice. It is evidence that the desktop was built not to remember.
### Section 4 What this closes and what it does not
**OBS** The premise is corrected: the desktop offers the choice in two surfaces,
since at least 2026-10-03 on this host, and shows which state is in force.
**UNK** The operator's preference. No source can answer it, and this round does not
pretend otherwise.
### Section 5 Divergence from the package text
The package's round-15 text dated the oldest dated copy 2026-10-06. This round's own
sweep of the same four copies dates the oldest 2026-10-03, and the count of copies
carrying the handler (4) agrees. The lane's measured figure is the one recorded here.
